scope: Proposition 4.2 (Pencil certificates for the original formula tree) of the manuscript “Polynomial Hitting Lists for Noncommutative Rational Formulas” (preprints/Polynomial-Hitting-Lists-for-Noncommutative-Rational-Formulas-September-24-2026/Polynomial-Hitting-Lists-for-Noncommutative-Rational-Formulas-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 116 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8f6fe5057bd59278), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 14-15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Φ be a formula of size at most s, and put B = 2s + 1. Form the indexed collection CΦ consisting of Lh for every inverse-node occurrence h of Φ, together with JΦ. Then: 1. The collection contains at most s + 1 affine pencils over Q, each of positive order at most B. 2. At every tuple of matrices of a common positive order over a field extension of Q, all pencils in CΦ are invertible if and only if the original formula tree Φ is defined there and its value is invertible. 14 3. If Φ is admissible and nonzero, there is a single tuple over some field extension of Q at which every pencil in CΦ is invertible. Adding the order-one constant pencil 1 for normalization gives at most s + 2 pencils, still of order at most B, with the same simultaneous feasibility property in the third assertion.
